statement: The first line holds n and k; the second holds n card values in a row. You must take exactly k cards, each from the left end or the right end of the row, scoring their sum. Print the maximum score. Flip the problem: the cards you leave form a contiguous window of fixed length n minus k, so the best play leaves the minimum-sum window of that length. Slide that fixed window across the row once, track its smallest sum, and subtract it from the total.

example.why: Taking 1, 6 and 5 from the right scores 12; the three left cards score only 6.

hint: Fixed width means no shrink logic: add the entering value, subtract the leaving one.
mistake: Greedily grabbing the bigger end card each turn - early picks can lock the best cards away.
